points.title: Tenses & Time Markers (時態與時間標記)
examples: 現在：簡單、進行、完成 (完成進行)
過去：簡單、進行、完成 (完成進行)
未來：簡單、進行、完成 (完成進行)
過去未來：簡單、進行、完成 (完成進行)

points.title: Transition Signals: Cause & Effect
examples: clause connectors: because, as, since, so
sentence connectors: therefore, thus, as a result, in consequence, consequently, for this reason
prepositional connectors: because of, due to, on account of, owing to, as a result of
verbs/phrasl verbs: cause, lead to, contritube to, result in, result from, give rise to, be caused by, arise from

items.sentence: The magnificence of Venice, which was built on the sea more than a thousand years ago, *sets* it apart from any other city in the world.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (which...) + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O + C

items.sentence: A prominent center of commerce in its early days, this Italian city *depended* largely on sea trade.
items.pattern: Participial phrase + S + Vi + Adverb + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Today, Venice's tranquil lagoons, ancient bridges, and vast web of canals *attract* tens of millions of visitors every year.
items.pattern: S (Compound subject) + Vt + O + Adverbial phrase

items.sentence: In recent years, however, Venice *has become* a city at risk, sinking and flooding as a result of both natural conditions and human activities.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vl + C + Participial phrase

items.sentence: Flooding in Venice *results* from two natural factors.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: One *is* acqua alta, which literally means "high water."
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: Acqua alta commonly *occurs* in winter, when a combination of high tides, strong winds, and large waves *causes* a huge volume of water to surge into the city.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Adverbial phrase + Adverbial clause (when...)

items.sentence: This, as one would expect, greatly *increases* the likelihood of flooding.
items.pattern: S + Adverb + Vt + O

items.sentence: The other factor *is* natural subsidence.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C

items.sentence: Venice *was constructed* on marshland and *lacks* a solid, stable foundation.
items.pattern: S + Vi / Vt (Compound predicate) + Prepositional phrase / O

items.sentence: In consequence, the city's buildings *have sunk* over time.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vi + Adverbial phrase

items.sentence: Venice's subsidence *is* also due to its location on top of the Adriatic Plate, which is gradually shifting beneath the Apennine Mountains.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: This shift *is causing* the land that Venice sits on to drop even further in elevation.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O with Relative clause (that...) + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: In addition to these natural forces, human actions also *threaten* Venice.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + O

items.sentence: In the 1930s, for industrial purposes, people *began* to pump out the water that helped to sustain and support this floating city.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrases + S + Vi + Infinitival O + Relative clause (that...)

items.sentence: This activity *caused* the rate of subsidence to accelerate dramatically throughout the rest of the 20th century.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Infinitival complement

items.sentence: Although pumping water was banned in the 1970s, considerable damage *had already been done*.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Although...) + S + Passive verb phrase

items.sentence: It *is estimated* that Venice has sunk by about 25 centimeters in the past century alone.
items.pattern: Passive reporting structure + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: As if land subsidence were not a serious enough problem, the city also *has to contend with* the effects of climate change.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (As if...) + S + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O

items.sentence: Since the start of the Industrial Revolution, humans *have burned* vast quantities of fossil fuels and thus *have released* excessive carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vt / Vt (Compound predicate) + Compound O

items.sentence: This process *has led* to global warming, which in turn has resulted in the melting of the polar ice caps and rising sea levels around the world.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Relative clause (which...)

items.sentence: Estimates that the overall water level in Venice will rise by as much as 53 centimeters by 2100 *appear* to confirm that climate change is having a very serious and dangerous impact indeed.
items.pattern: S + Noun clause (that...) + Vi + Infinitival phrase + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: The natural factors and human actions mentioned *have combined* to cause frequent flooding in Venice, and the situation *is* only getting worse.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Infinitival phrase + and + S + Vl + C

items.sentence: As a matter of fact, in the past century alone, the incidence of flooding *has increased* from fewer than 10 times a year to more than 60!
items.pattern: Adverbial phrases + S + Vi + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: If this scenario seems hard to imagine, *take* a glimpse back in history.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) + Imperative sentence

items.sentence: In November 1966, a high tide *swept* into Venice, causing a flood that reached an extraordinary height of 194 centimeters and submerged the city for 22 hours.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vi + Participial phrase + Relative clause (that...) with compound verbs

items.sentence: This flood, the highest on record, *was nearly matched* in 2019, when the water level rose to 187 centimeters.
items.pattern: S + Appositive phrase + Passive verb phrase + Adverbial clause (when...)

items.sentence: Although this latter instance of flooding was not quite as severe as the 1966 event, it *should be noted* that it marked the first of five instances that year when flood waters in the city reached heights of over 140 centimeters.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Although...) + Passive reporting structure + Noun clause (that...) + Relative clause (when...)

items.sentence: In response, the Italian government *has introduced* the MOSE, a system of movable barriers to block seawater during high tides.
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vt + O + Appositive phrase

items.sentence: As the world's sea levels continue to rise, largely owing to human actions, the outlook for Venice *remains* uncertain despite ongoing protective efforts.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (As...) + S + Vl + C + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Indeed, the case of Venice *offers* a test for humanity - a test of whether we can make the joint efforts needed to curb global warming and prevent the environment from being destroyed.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Appositive phrase + Noun clause (whether...) + Infinitival phrases

items.sentence: Such efforts *are* far from being the responsibility of only individual governments or groups.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: Instead, they *require* all humans to acknowledge what is happening and to work toward the common goal of preserving our beloved Earth for future generations.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Infinitival phrases + Noun clause (what...)
